fields.explanation: The source defines S_k as binomially normalized averages, whereas the old narrative called them raw sums. With the same F values(1,1,−1,−1), both have values(1,0,−1), so the witness is unchanged. Mathlib Finset cardinality layers and Nat.choose now express the actual normalized averages and real absolute-value inequality.
fields.flaw: Every real-valued function F on the subsets of <n> with F(φ)=1 that satisfies F(α∩β)F(α∪β)≤F(α)F(β) for all α,β⊆<n> also satisfies (S_k^F)^2≥|S_{k-1}^F S_{k+1}^F| for 1≤k<n.
fields.problem: Title: Newton's Inequalities on a Lattice
fields.witness: Take n=2 on {0,1}: F(∅)=1, F({0})=1, F({1})=−1, F({0,1})=−1. Using the source definition S_k^F=(1/binom(2,k))∑_{|A|=k}F(A), the normalized averages are S_0=1, S_1=0, S_2=−1. Thus the k=1 conclusion says 0≥1, which is false.
